phases.Glomerular filtration: Plasma is filtered from the glomerular capillaries into Bowman's space by a net filtration pressure of 10 mmHg (55 − 15 − 30); the parcel starts as 300 mOsm/kg filtrate.
phases.Proximal convoluted tubule: Iso-osmotic reabsorption: Na⁺ is pumped out and water follows, so ~65% of the volume leaves while osmolality stays 300; all glucose and most bicarbonate are reclaimed.
phases.Thin descending limb: Water-only wall: water leaves into the increasingly salty medulla, so the fluid concentrates to ~1200 mOsm/kg at the loop tip.
phases.Thick ascending limb: Water-tight wall: NKCC2 pumps NaCl out, so the fluid dilutes (to ~100) while the interstitium is kept salty; the single effect that builds the gradient.
phases.Distal convoluted tubule: NCC (thiazide-sensitive) removes more NaCl with no water; the fluid becomes most dilute; the macula densa sits at its start.
phases.Cortical collecting duct: Principal cells: aldosterone drives ENaC Na⁺ uptake and K⁺ secretion; with ADH, water leaves and the fluid returns to ~300.
phases.Medullary collecting duct: With ADH (AQP2), water leaves into the deep medulla so the urine concentrates toward ~1200 mOsm/kg, with under 1% of the filtrate left.

parts.aff: Afferent arteriole: brings blood into the glomerulus; its pressure sets glomerular capillary pressure.
parts.glom: Glomerular capillary tuft where plasma is filtered.
parts.eff: Efferent arteriole: carries blood out of the glomerulus into the peritubular capillaries and vasa recta.
parts.bowman: Bowman's capsule: collects the filtrate; its pressure (15 mmHg) opposes filtration.
parts.pct: Proximal convoluted tubule with brush border: bulk iso-osmotic reabsorption (Na⁺, water, glucose, HCO₃⁻).
parts.tdl: Thin descending limb: permeable to water (AQP1), not salt.
parts.tal: Thick ascending limb: NKCC2 salt pump, impermeable to water; target of loop diuretics.
parts.md: Macula densa: tall cells of the late thick limb that sense NaCl delivery next to the glomerulus (tubuloglomerular feedback).
parts.dct: Distal convoluted tubule: NCC salt uptake, water-tight; target of thiazides.
parts.cd: Collecting duct: aldosterone (ENaC, ROMK) and ADH-controlled water reabsorption (AQP2); sets final urine concentration.
parts.ptc: Peritubular capillaries: take back what the cortical tubule reabsorbs.
parts.vr: Vasa recta: hairpin capillaries in the medulla that supply it without washing out the gradient (countercurrent exchange).
parts.interstitium: Medullary interstitium: osmolality rising from 300 at the corticomedullary border to 1200 at the papilla.

readouts.osm: Osmolality of the tubular fluid in the parcel right now.
readouts.vol: Percentage of the original filtrate volume still left in the tubule.
readouts.intOsm: Osmolality of the interstitium around the parcel at its current depth.
readouts.flowDay: Tubular flow at this point scaled to both kidneys, in litres per day.
readouts.gap: Tubular fluid minus interstitial osmolality: negative means the fluid is more dilute than its surroundings.
readouts.waterOut: Rate at which water is leaving the parcel.
readouts.saltOut: Rate at which solute is leaving the parcel.
readouts.glucose: Percentage of filtered glucose still in the tubule.
readouts.hco3: Percentage of filtered bicarbonate still in the tubule.
readouts.depth: How deep the parcel is in the medulla (0 = corticomedullary border, 1 = papilla tip; negative = cortex).
readouts.nfp: Net filtration pressure across the glomerular membrane.

concepts: sites of action of diuretics (loop, thiazide)
